dedupe_keys.name: taiwan integrated cost benefit framework and financial cost model for municipal solid waste management systems

description: This case study builds a framework for judging how cost-effective municipal solid waste management systems are and applies its financial part to Taiwan. Yu-Chi Weng and Takeshi Fujiwara of the Solid Waste Management Research Center at Okayama University published it in Waste Management in 2011. The authors first set out an integrated cost-benefit analysis framework that spells out the detailed costs and benefits caused by waste problems, meant for municipal decision-makers and citizens. They then develop a general method for evaluating the financial cost-effectiveness of waste systems that accounts for treatment technology levels and policy effects, analyse how these factors drive annual total and average operation and maintenance costs in Taiwan, and make a short-term projection of financial costs under scenarios. The article is available online by subscription, and the abstract is free on PubMed. Coverage is national. Caveats: only the financial cost side was quantified for Taiwan, and the data behind the projection are not published. Simulation uses: a cost structure linking technology and policy to waste system operating costs for municipal waste planning models. Related records: the Taiwan municipal waste account replication package (data-replication-package-for-overtaken-but-overloaded-a-moving-reporting-boundary-conceals-a-capacity-crisis-in-tai-p02964) gives open data on Taiwan's municipal waste.
